newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine police blame Moslem rebels for butchery.
newsitem.headline: Philippine police blame Moslem rebels for butchery.

text.p: Five members of a coconut farming family were hacked to death in front of their female relatives on this southern Philippine island, in what police said was the work of Moslem rebels.

Peter Mosquera, his two sons and two other relatives were tied up and killed in front of his wife and daughter, who were briefly abducted, local police chief Constantino Sayson told reporters on Monday.

"We were screaming for mercy as they hacked our family like butchers. They didn't have any pity, because they even set fire to our house," he quoted Mosquera's wife as telling police after she was rescued.
One of the men, all Christians, was beheaded.
The heavily-armed teenagers broke into her house in the early hours of Sunday morning.

She said they were members of the extremist Moslem rebel group Abu Sayyaf. She said her family was suspected of spying on Abu Sayyaf for the military and had also refused to pay the group a "revolutionary tax" for protection.
The group's stronghold is in the southern island of Basilan where it is fighting for independence from the predominantly-Christian Philippines.
But the Philippine military says they have degenerated into little more than bandits, elusive in their mountain enclaves.

"They are preoccupied with extortion, kidnapping and other criminal activities, and have basically turned into criminal bandits that have stymied the economic growth (of their region)," armed forces commander Arnulfo Acedera said in a speech last week.
